insert.title: How IndexMap::insert() works
insert.description: Adds a key and value; the map remembers the order keys were inserted.

slides.caption: An IndexMap stores its entries in a Vec, in insertion order, plus a hash table that points into that Vec.
"c" is new: it goes to the end, at index 0. insert() returns None.
Iterating gives c, a, b: the insertion order. A HashMap would give an order you cannot predict. Inserting "a" again would replace its value and keep it at index 1.
m.keys() yields c, a, b. Lookups by key are still as fast as in a HashMap.

get-index.title: How IndexMap::get_index() works
get-index.description: Looks up an entry by its position.

slides.caption: get_index() reads the entry stored at a position, like indexing a Vec.
It returns both the key and the value, as Some((&key, &value)).
An index past the end, like get_index(3), returns None instead of panicking.
m.get_index(1) is Some(("a", 2)). Positions change when entries are removed with swap_remove() or shift_remove().

get-index-of.title: How IndexMap::get_index_of() works
get-index-of.description: Finds the position of a key.

slides.caption: get_index_of() is the opposite of get_index(): it takes a key and returns its position.
The hash table finds "b" directly, without walking the entries.
That entry is stored at index 2.
A key that is not in the map, like "z", gives None.
m.get_index_of("b") is Some(2). get_full("b") returns the index, the key and the value together.

swap-remove.title: How IndexMap::swap_remove() works
swap-remove.description: Removes an entry fast by moving the last entry into its place; the order changes.

slides.caption: swap_remove() removes an entry without shifting the others. That is fast, but it changes the order.
"c" is at index 0. It is taken out and its value 1 is returned.
The gap is filled with the last entry: "b" moves from index 2 to index 0.
Only one entry moved, whatever the size of the map. "a" kept its index; "b" did not.
After swap_remove("c") the keys are b, a. Use shift_remove() when the order must be kept.

shift-remove.title: How IndexMap::shift_remove() works
shift-remove.description: Removes an entry and shifts the later entries down, keeping the order.

slides.caption: shift_remove() removes an entry like Vec::remove(): everything after it moves one place to the left.
"c" at index 0 is taken out; its value 1 is returned.
"a" moves from index 1 to 0 and "b" from 2 to 1.
The order is kept, but every later entry had to move: slower than swap_remove() for big maps.
After shift_remove("c") the keys are a, b. In indexmap 1.x, plain remove() was swap_remove().

sort-keys.title: How IndexMap::sort_keys() works
sort-keys.description: Sorts the entries of the map by key, in place.

slides.caption: sort_keys() reorders the entries so that the keys are in ascending order. The values move with their keys.
"a" is the smallest key: it moves to index 0.
The map now iterates a, b, c, and get_index(0) is ("a", 2). sort_by() takes your own comparison.

set-insert.title: How IndexSet::insert() works
set-insert.description: Adds a value to a set that keeps insertion order; returns false for a value already in it.

note.text: a set: each value at most once, in insertion order

slides.caption: IndexSet is an IndexMap without values. insert() returns true when the value was new.
"b" is new: it is added at index 0 and insert() returns true.
"b" is already in the set: nothing is added, it keeps index 0, and insert() returns false.
The set iterates b, a and the three calls returned true, true, false. insert_full() also returns the index.

map-new.title: How IndexMap::new works
map-new.description: An empty map that remembers the order keys were inserted in.

slides.caption: IndexMap iterates in insertion order and also lets you access entries by position.
Lookups by key are as fast as a HashMap.

map-get.title: How IndexMap::get works
map-get.description: Looks up a value by key.

map-get-mut.title: How IndexMap::get_mut works
map-get-mut.description: A mutable reference to a value by key.

map-entry.title: How IndexMap::entry works
map-entry.description: The entry for a key, to insert or update with one lookup.

slides.caption: New keys are added at the end.

map-iter.title: How IndexMap::iter works
map-iter.description: Iterates (key, value) pairs in insertion order.

slides.caption: This order is the main reason to use IndexMap.
keys() and values() follow the same order.

map-pop.title: How IndexMap::pop works
map-pop.description: Removes and returns the last entry.

map-retain.title: How IndexMap::retain works
map-retain.description: Keeps only the entries the closure approves, preserving order.

slides.caption: Order of the survivors is kept.

map-sort-by.title: How IndexMap::sort_by works
map-sort-by.description: Reorders the entries with a comparison of (key, value) pairs.

slides.caption: The closure gets key1, value1, key2, value2.

map-sort-unstable-keys.title: How IndexMap::sort_unstable_keys works
map-sort-unstable-keys.description: Sorts the entries by key with an unstable sort.

slides.caption: Keys are unique, so stability does not matter here.

map-sorted-by.title: How IndexMap::sorted_by works
map-sorted-by.description: Consumes the map and returns its entries sorted, as an iterator.

map-reverse.title: How IndexMap::reverse works
map-reverse.description: Reverses the order of the entries.

slides.caption: iter().rev() iterates backwards without changing it.

map-get-full.title: How IndexMap::get_full works
map-get-full.description: The position, key and value for a key, in one lookup.

map-insert-full.title: How IndexMap::insert_full works
map-insert-full.description: Inserts and tells you the position and the old value.

slides.caption: An existing key keeps its position.

map-move-index.title: How IndexMap::move_index works
map-move-index.description: Moves the entry at one position to another.

slides.caption: Entries in between shift by one.

map-swap-indices.title: How IndexMap::swap_indices works
map-swap-indices.description: Swaps the entries at two positions.

slides.caption: O(1) apart from the index bookkeeping.

map-shift-remove-index.title: How IndexMap::shift_remove_index works
map-shift-remove-index.description: Removes the entry at a position, keeping the order of the rest.

map-swap-remove-index.title: How IndexMap::swap_remove_index works
map-swap-remove-index.description: Removes the entry at a position; the last entry takes its place.

map-truncate.title: How IndexMap::truncate works
map-truncate.description: Keeps only the first n entries.

slides.caption: Removes from the end, so it is cheap.

map-split-off.title: How IndexMap::split_off works
map-split-off.description: Splits the map at a position; the tail becomes a new map.

map-drain.title: How IndexMap::drain works
map-drain.description: Removes a range of entries and yields them.

slides.caption: Positions after the range shift down.

map-get-index-mut.title: How IndexMap::get_index_mut works
map-get-index-mut.description: The key and a mutable value at a position.

slides.caption: The key is returned too, but read-only.

map-binary-search-keys.title: How IndexMap::binary_search_keys works
map-binary-search-keys.description: Binary search by key in a map whose keys are sorted.

slides.caption: Err(pos) says where the key would go.
Only correct if the keys are sorted.

set-contains.title: How IndexSet::contains works
set-contains.description: true if the value is in the set.

set-get-index-of.title: How IndexSet::get_index_of works
set-get-index-of.description: The position of a value in the set.

set-shift-remove.title: How IndexSet::shift_remove works
set-shift-remove.description: Removes a value, keeping the order of the rest.

slides.caption: y and z keep their order.

set-union.title: How IndexSet::union works
set-union.description: Values in either set: this set's order first, then the other's new values.

slides.caption: Lazily iterates; collect to keep it.
Then the new ones from b.

set-intersection.title: How IndexSet::intersection works
set-intersection.description: Values in both sets, in this set's order.

slides.caption: difference keeps those not in b.

set-insert-full.title: How IndexSet::insert_full works
set-insert-full.description: Inserts and returns (position, was it new).

slides.caption: An existing value keeps its position.
A new value goes at the end.

set-pop.title: How IndexSet::pop works
set-pop.description: Removes and returns the last value.

slides.caption: Good for ordered work queues without duplicates.

map-shift-insert.title: How IndexMap::shift_insert works
map-shift-insert.description: Inserts a key at a given position, shifting later entries.

slides.caption: An existing key is moved to that position.

map-append.title: How IndexMap::append works
map-append.description: Moves all entries of another map to the end of this one.

slides.caption: other is left empty; existing keys keep their position.
